strongest_results: The common-success high-Q star has rational-angle edge density at most n^(-2/15+o(1)), yielding pairwise-irrational and three-source-general-position subfamilies of sizes n^(2/15-o(1)) and n^(1/10-o(1)).

For an n-point three-dimensional set with D distances, the number of same-orientation R-rich rigid motions is O(n^4(D log n)^(4/3)/R^3) once R is at least a constant times D log n. At D=n^(3/5+o(1)), R=n^(1-o(1)), this is n^(9/5+o(1)).

The rich-motion bound shortens the general-position word thresholds to L=19 for positive multiplicity and L=28 for near-linear multiplicity, and gives t^(2L-18-o(1)) pushforward word energy without claiming small tripling of the generator set.

On almost the full n^(4/5-o(1)) star, adjacent irrational turns produce n^(3/5-o(1)) same-motion, same-endpoint three-reflection representations and hence genuine nonempty relations of length at most six.
A fixed-axis Q-rich plane-pencil bound extracts n^(1/5-o(1)) distinct n^(1-o(1))-rich infinite-order rotations h_a=g s_a in one reflection coset.

The coset is classified into reflection/coplanar-axis, glide/parallel-axis, or unique-fixed-point/concurrent-axis geometry. In the glide and fixed-point branches, independent affine-complex and projective-quaternion point-line models bound T-plane representation counts by O(T^(4/3)+T), forcing T>=n^(9/20-o(1)) and equally large coplanar or cospherical P-point witnesses.

In the reflection branch, either an n^(1/5-o(1)) plane pencil or n^(1/5-o(1)) active coplanar axes occurs. The local angular relation has Theta(m^2) irrational-turn solutions, so no analogous purely algebraic 4/3 saving is possible; an exact circular-fibre q_alpha/r_alpha model identifies the missing joint weighted-energy estimate.

The low-Q route retains both q_pi and generating-pair weight g_pi, proves pinned irrational/general-position subfamilies and a source-sensitive triple-codegree bound, but its unweighted moments remain below contradiction scale.
results.remaining_gap: For glide and fixed-point branches, prove an o(n^(9/20)) bound for Q-rich source planes whose reflections and common-coset rotations are simultaneously n^(1-o(1))-rich. For the reflection branch, prove o(n^(1/5)) for the synchronized coplanar-axis rich rotations using the joint Q-rich/circular-autocorrelation data. The low-Q weighted branch and the all-fixed-d lift also remain open.

strongest_results: For each fixed 0<eta<=1/12, either there is an Omega(N^(1/4+eta)) circumradius-rainbow subset, one radius supports Omega(N^(7/4-5eta)) triangles, or Omega(N^(1-4eta)) centers each support an Omega(N^(1-4eta)) pinned tangent matching.
The multi-center branch forces two centers with Omega(N^(1-8eta)) common matching endpoints and, more generally, j fixed centers with Omega(N^(1-4j eta)) common endpoints whenever 4j eta<=1.
The matching partners may lie outside the common endpoint core and the selected radii may differ, so these concentration statements do not yield a new H5/H6 power saving or n_k exponent.
results.remaining_gap: Prove a source-sensitive semi-algebraic incidence saving for multiple inversion centers, common endpoints, and their separate secant partners, or solve the competing #104-rich radius branch with a fixed power saving.

publication_assessment.assessment: The n^(9/5+o(1)) rich-motion bound and n^(9/20-o(1)) two-branch concentration are the strongest internally rigorous reusable/structural outputs, but neither changes a recognized original-problem exponent. Exhaustive novelty and priority review was not completed, so no SCI Q2 claim is made.
